atoms.sound: Hey, everyone. Let’s start our book club meeting. We need to choose our next book. Do you have any ideas?
Yes, I brought some books from the library, but I’m not sure what they’re about.
The cover usually gives clues about what kind of story it is. Let’s look at them together.

instruction.text: Match the book covers to the correct descriptions.

atoms.sound: Now we have three books to think about. Maybe we should each talk about which one we like. It might help us decide. Do you want to start, Ana?

Sure! The romance novel isn’t really my thing, but I’m interested in the fantasy book, the one about the teenage witch. The back cover says that she finds a spell book that changes her whole summer. I like magic stories and this one sounds fun. What about you, Reece?

I like the science-fiction book, The Last Planet. It’s about a group of young explorers who land on a new planet after their ship breaks down. They have to work together to survive, and they discover something strange there. I enjoy stories with adventure and new worlds. I definitely don’t want to read a romance novel. What do you think, Noor?
I agree. I don’t really like romances either. So we can take that one off the list. I like both other options.

instruction.text: Which book are they not going to read?

atoms.sound: So we only have two books left. How do we choose between them?
Maybe we should read a review for each one.
Great idea! I searched for reviews and I found the top one for each book.

b: ++Magic After Midnight has an interesting main character.
Both reviews say the books are slow and not interesting.
++The Last Planet asks big questions about being human.
The reviewer thinks Magic After Midnight has a strong ending.

atoms.a: How does the reviewer feel about the fantasy book overall?
b: ++They think it has good and weak parts.
They think it is perfect.

atoms.sound: After reading the reviews, I think The Last Planet sounds much more interesting.
I agree. The review for the fantasy book was mixed, but The Last Planet sounds great.
I would read both books to be honest, but I’m happy to choose the one the two of you prefer.
